text.S1: Once upon a time there were four little Rabbits, and their names were Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter.
text.S2: Once there lived four little Rabbits namely Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter.
text.T1: Nako yeñwi nekuna ni tushakame totune totubizwa Fulopusi, Mopusi, Kotoni-teilu ni Pita.

text.S1: They lived with their mother in a sand-bank, underneath the root of a very big fir-tree.
text.S2: They kept up with their mother in sand covered by shallow water underneath the root of a very big fir-tree.
text.T1: ‘Netupila ni bo maatona mwa muuwa kwatasaa mubisi wa kota yetuna yebizwa ka sikuwa kuli ‘fir.’ T 2: ‘Netupila ni bo maatona mwa muuwa kwatasaa mubisi wa kota yetuna yebizwa ka Sikuwa kuli ‘fir.’ T3 Netupila ni bo matona mwa muuwa kwatasaa mubisi wa kota yetuna yebizwa ka sikuwa kuli ‘fir.’

text.S1: 'Now my dears,' said old Mrs. Rabbit one morning, 'you may go into the fields or down the lane, but don't go into Mr. McGregor's garden: your Father had accident there; he was put in a pie by Mrs. McGregor.'
text.S2: “My dearest children,” said their old mother, Mrs. Rabbit one morning. “You can go into the gardens or down the road, but don't go into Mr. McGregor's garden because your father had an accident there as he was put in a pie by Mrs. McGregor.”
text.T1: “Cwale balatiwa baaka,” kakusasana omuñwi musalaa Shakame wa mucembele abulela. Aekeza hape ali, “Mwakona kuya mwa simu kapa kushetumuka mwa nzila, kono musike mwaya mwa simu ya bo McGregor kakuli bo ndataamina bakile baba ni kozi mwateñi. neba beilwe mwa sikono ki mufumahali wa bo McGregor.”

text.S1: 'Now run along, and don't get into mischief. I am going out.'

text.S1: Then old Mrs. Rabbit took a basket and her umbrella, and went through the wood to the baker's. She bought a loaf of brown bread and five currant buns.
text.S2: Mrs. Rabbit’s old wife started off to the bakery carrying her basket and an ambrella, passing through the bush. She bought herself a loaf of brown bread and five currant buns.

text.S2: Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter who were well behaved rabbits, descended the road to the gardens to pluck blackberries.

text.S1: But Peter, who was very naughty, ran straight away to Mr. McGregor's garden, and squeezed under the gate!
text.S2: However, Peter who was a very naughty boy ran straight to Mr. McGregor's garden, and passed under the gate to enter!

text.S2: He started eating leaves of lettuce plants and some French beans then radishes.

text.S1: Mr. McGregor was on his hands and knees planting out young cabbages, but he jumped up and ran after Peter, waving a rake and calling out, 'Stop thief!'
text.S2: Mr. McGregor was squating, busy planting his cabbage seedilings. Suddenly, he jumped and chased Peter while lifting his rake high as he shouted, “Thief stop!”
text.T1: Bo McGregor neba kubami banze basweli kucala kabici yenyinyani, kapilipili batulela mwahalimu ni kukala kumatisa Pita banze bazukuza hala yabona mwahalimu ni kuhuwa bali, “Lisholi yema!”
text.T2: Bo McGregor neba kubami banze basweli kucala kabici yenyinyani, kapilipili batulela mwahalimu ni kukala kumatisa Pita banze bazukuza hala yabona mwahalimu ni kuhuwa bali, “Lisholi yema!”

text.S1: Peter was most dreadfully frightened; he rushed all over the garden, for he had forgotten the way back to the gate. He lost one of his shoes among the cabbages, and the other shoe amongst the potatoes.
text.S2: Peter was very scared as he was not sure of where the exit gate was located. He missed the way to the gate so he was just running round and round the garden. In the process, one of his pair of shoes was lost among the plants of cabbage while the other shoe got lost among the plants of potatoes.

text.S1: After losing them, he ran on four legs and went faster, so that I think he might have got away altogether if he had not unfortunately run into a gooseberry net, and got caught by the large buttons on his jacket. It was a blue jacket with brass buttons, quite new.
text.S2: After his pair of shoes had been lost, he ran faster on his two legs and two hands. I feel that he would have escaped had it not been for the unfortunate episode of running into a gooseberry shrub net which hooked him by the large buttons of his jacket and was caught. It was a quite new blue jacket with shining brass buttons.

text.S2: Mr. McGregor came up with a sieve, which he intended to cover Peter’s head with, but Peter resisted very strongly and pulled out just in time, leaving his jacket behind him.

text.S1: And rushed into the tool-shed, and jumped into a can. It would have been a beautiful thing to hide in, if it had not had so much water in it.
text.S2: He quickly ran to the tool-shed, jumped into a can and hid himself there. If the can had no much water, It would have been a better place to hide in.

text.S1: Mr. McGregor was quite sure that Peter was somewhere in the tool-shed, perhaps hidden underneath a flower-pot. He began to turn them over carefully, looking under each. Presently Peter sneezed—'Kertyschoo!' Mr. McGregor was after him in no time.
text.S2: Mr. McGregor believed that Peter was in the tool-shed and was hiding underneath the flower pots. He began to arrange the flower pots in the upside down positions while carefully observing under each flower pot. Suddenly, Peter sneezed and the sound was heard, “Kertyschoo!” Mr. McGregor was on him in no time at all.

text.S1: And tried to put his foot upon Peter who jumped out of a window, upsetting three plants. The window was too small for Mr. McGregor, and he was tired of running after Peter. He went back to his work.

text.S1: Peter sat down to rest; he was out of breath and trembling with fright, and he had not the least idea which way to go. Also he was very damp with sitting in that can. After a time he began to wander about, going lippity—lippity—not very fast, and looking all round.
text.S2: Peter sat down to rest. He breathed hard and trembled by fear. He had no idea of which direction to go. He was damp because of sitting in that can of water. Afterwards, he began to slowly wonder and look around.

text.S1: He found a door in a wall; but it was locked, and there was no room for a fat little rabbit to squeeze underneath. An old mouse was running in and out over the stone doorstep, carrying peas and beans to her family in the wood. Peter asked her the way to the gate, but she had such a large pea in her mouth that she could not answer. She only shook her head at him. Peter began to cry.

text.S1: Then he tried to find his way straight across the garden, but he became more and more puzzled. Presently, he came to a pond where Mr. McGregor filled his water-cans. A white cat was staring at some gold-fish. She sat very, very still, but now and then the tip of her tail twitched as if it were alive. Peter thought it best to go away without speaking to her; he had heard about cats from his cousin, little Benjamin Bunny.
text.S2: Then he tried to find his way by cutting straight across the garden although he was puzzled. Suddenly, he arrived at a pond where Mr. McGregor had filled up his cans of water. A white cat was standing still, staring at some gold-fish. However, the tip of her tail twitched to indicate that was alive. Peter thought it was wise to just go away without speaking to her. He had heard stories about cats from his cousin called little Benjamin Bunny.

text.S1: He went back towards the toolshed, but suddenly, quite close to him, he heard the noise of a hoe scratch, scratch, scratch, scratch, scritch. Peter took cover in the bushes. But presently, as nothing happened, he came out, and climbed upon a wheelbarrow and peeped over. The first thing he saw was Mr. McGregor hoeing onions. His back was turned towards Peter, and beyond him was the gate!

text.T1: Akuta ka kuliba kwa libulukelo la lisebeliso, kono kapilipili, bukaufi ni fanaa inzi, autwa mulumo wa muhuma haulima uli, “Caku! Caku! Caku!” Pita ki hai pata mwatasaa macecani. Kono honafo inge hakuna sene siezahalile, aipatulula, ni kupahama fahalimu a ngolobani kunangela. Nto yapili yanaa boni neeli bo McGregor inge balima nyanisi. Neba fulalezi Pita mi kwapili yabona nekuna ni munyako wa lukwakwa!

Kono honafo inge hakuna sene siezahalile, aipatulula, ni kupahama fahalimu a ngolobani kunangela. Nto yapili yanaa boni neeli bo McGregor inge balima nyanisi. text.S1: Peter got down very quietly off the wheelbarrow; and started run- ning as fast as he could go, along a straight walk behind some black- currant bushes. Mr. McGregor caught sight of him at the corner, but Peter did not care. He slipped underneath the gate, and was safe at last in the wood outside the garden.

text.S1: He was so tired that he flopped down upon the nice soft sand on the floor of the rabbit-hole and shut his eyes. His mother was busy cooking; she wondered what he had done with his clothes. It was the second little jacket and pair of shoes that Peter had lost in a fort-night!
